title: Add a guarded keyboard shortcut for replaying the last failed request
before: At parent commit 6fdd7154587c731fbffaf416cb20b8336b52b662, the command registry and default key bindings had no retry-last command, InputPrompt did not dispatch a retry action, UIActions exposed no retry handler, and the request-stream hook neither retained the last prepared prompt nor tracked whether it failed. after: At c353fbbfa3d7418920044fd194c53c970624955f, Ctrl+Y is registered as a RETRY_LAST command and dispatched by InputPrompt through UIActions to retryLastPrompt. Error items can carry an inline localized retry hint, and shortcut documentation/discovery surfaces include the new command.
diff: The implementation adds a semantic retry-last command and Ctrl+Y binding; threads a retry callback from useGeminiStream through AppContainer and UIActionsContext into InputPrompt; records the last prepared prompt and its failure state; implements guarded replay with pending-error/history reconciliation and skipPreparation; extends error history items and rendering with optional inline hints; updates shortcut discovery, localization, and documentation; and adds matcher and input-path tests plus adjustments to retry-error/countdown tests.

- Add Ctrl+Y keyboard shortcut for retrying the last failed request
- Add isNetworkError() to detect transient network failures (ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, etc.)
- Add DashScope 1305 error code to rate limit detection
- Add error hint \"Press Ctrl+Y to retry\" in error messages
- Support user-defined error codes for retry via config
- Add retryLastPrompt() hook in useGeminiStream
- Update keyboard shortcuts documentation

* feat: improve Ctrl+Y retry feature with tests, docs, and rate limit config

- Add comprehensive tests for Ctrl+Y retry shortcut in InputPrompt
- Add unit tests for retryLastPrompt in useGeminiStream hook
- Add detailed JSDoc comments for retryLastPrompt function and Ctrl+Y shortcut
- Extend isRateLimitError to support custom error codes via retryErrorCodes config
- Fix rate limit retry log variable reference (RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_OPTIONS → maxRateLimitRetries)
- Add Eclipse IDE files to .gitignore

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* refactor(ui): consolidate retry countdown as inline hint in error messages

episode.title: Add a guarded keyboard shortcut for replaying the last failed request
episode.before: At parent commit 6fdd7154587c731fbffaf416cb20b8336b52b662, the command registry and default key bindings had no retry-last command, InputPrompt did not dispatch a retry action, UIActions exposed no retry handler, and the request-stream hook neither retained the last prepared prompt nor tracked whether it failed. Errors were committed directly to history without a removable manual-retry hint, so a failed request could not be replayed through a dedicated shortcut.
episode.after: At c353fbbfa3d7418920044fd194c53c970624955f, Ctrl+Y is registered as a RETRY_LAST command and dispatched by InputPrompt through UIActions to retryLastPrompt. The stream hook retains the last prepared prompt, records whether it failed, refuses replay while responding or awaiting confirmation, reports when no failed request exists, commits the prior error without its transient hint, clears retry UI/countdown state, and resubmits the stored prompt while bypassing preparation. Error items can carry an inline localized retry hint, and shortcut documentation/discovery surfaces include the new command.
episode.diff: The implementation adds a semantic retry-last command and Ctrl+Y binding; threads a retry callback from useGeminiStream through AppContainer and UIActionsContext into InputPrompt; records the last prepared prompt and its failure state; implements guarded replay with pending-error/history reconciliation and skipPreparation; extends error history items and rendering with optional inline hints; updates shortcut discovery, localization, and documentation; and adds matcher and input-path tests plus adjustments to retry-error/countdown tests.

evidence_units.claim: Commit c353fbbfa3d7418920044fd194c53c970624955f is the implementation-bearing resolution linked to issue/PR 2011 and has parent 6fdd7154587c731fbffaf416cb20b8336b52b662.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller c353fbbfa3d7418920044fd194c53c970624955f; issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits and parent_commit

evidence_units.claim: The parent had no RETRY_LAST command or Ctrl+Y binding; the change adds Command.RETRY_LAST and maps it to key 'y' with ctrl true.
InputPrompt checks the normalized RETRY_LAST matcher, calls the UI retry action, and returns before later input handlers can consume the event.
The retry operation is exposed as handleRetryLastPrompt in UIActions, supplied by AppContainer from useGeminiStream.retryLastPrompt, and consumed by InputPrompt.

The stream hook adds refs for the last prepared prompt and whether it errored, stores the final prepared query before sending it, marks failures on streamed and thrown errors, and resets the failure flag on successful completion or a new submission.

retryLastPrompt is a guarded operation: it does nothing while responding or waiting for confirmation, emits an informational message when there is no stored failed prompt, and only otherwise proceeds with replay.

Before replay, retryLastPrompt commits the pending error text without its transient hint, clears pending retry/countdown state, and resubmits the stored prompt as a non-continuation with skipPreparation enabled.
submitQuery gains a skipPreparation option that sends the supplied stored query directly instead of invoking prepareQueryForGemini, allowing replay of the already-prepared prompt.

Error history items gain an optional hint; HistoryItemDisplay passes it to ErrorMessage, which renders it inline in secondary color, while failure paths keep the hinted error pending so the hint can be removed during retry.
The key-matcher table tests Ctrl+Y as a positive RETRY_LAST match and plain Y and Ctrl+R as negative matches, establishing modifier normalization and non-conflict with reverse search.

InputPrompt tests exercise the Ctrl+Y byte path and verify that plain Y remains normal input and Ctrl+R remains distinct; however, the positive Ctrl+Y case does not assert that handleRetryLastPrompt was called.

Stream-hook tests assert that retry errors are represented as pending error items with inline countdown hints, update as timers advance, and are cleared after successful automatic retry; another error-path test verifies a pending error item is created.
The visible shortcut list, localized strings, and user reference document describe Ctrl+Y as retrying the last failed request and provide messages for retry availability.

candidate_atomics.name: register-and-dispatch-semantic-shortcut
candidate_atomics.title: Register and dispatch a conflict-free semantic shortcut
candidate_atomics.description: Represent the shortcut as a named command, match the normalized key event including its modifier, and dispatch the corresponding UI action before unrelated input handlers run.

semantic_action.intent: Make one modified key sequence invoke a dedicated application action without treating the unmodified key or an existing shortcut as equivalent.
semantic_action.pre_state: The desired action has no semantic command binding and the input component has no dispatch branch for it.
semantic_action.post_state: The configured modified key matches exactly one semantic command, dispatches its UI action, and returns before later handlers; nearby unmodified and pre-existing shortcut events retain their behavior.
semantic_action.validation: Run matcher tests proving the intended modified key is positive and plain/conflicting keys are negative, then exercise the focused input path and assert the semantic action is invoked exactly once.

candidate_atomics.name: capture-failed-operation-for-guarded-replay
candidate_atomics.title: Capture the last failed operation and guard its replay
candidate_atomics.description: Retain the prepared request and explicit failure state, then admit replay only when a failed request exists and no active response or confirmation flow would conflict.

semantic_action.intent: Allow a user-triggered replay to target the exact last failed operation while preventing stale, absent, or concurrent replay.
semantic_action.pre_state: Requests are submitted without a retained replay target or explicit last-failure predicate, so the shortcut cannot safely determine what to replay.
semantic_action.post_state: The latest prepared request and its failure status are retained, successful/new execution resets stale failure state, active execution states block replay, and missing eligibility produces a user-visible no-op result.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise failure, success, missing-target, responding, and waiting-for-confirmation states; prove replay is admitted only for an idle controller holding a failed prepared request.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-retry-ui-and-replay-request
candidate_atomics.title: Reconcile transient error UI before replaying the stored request
candidate_atomics.description: Preserve actionable failure feedback as transient state, commit durable error text without the hint, clear retry/countdown artifacts, and replay the already-prepared request once.

semantic_action.intent: Replay an eligible failed request without duplicating transient hints, losing the error record, or reapplying initial prompt preparation.
semantic_action.module_role: retry-state reconciliation and request submission boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: An eligible failed prepared request exists, with an error and optional retry/countdown affordance held in mutable pending UI state.
semantic_action.post_state: The durable history contains the error text without the transient hint, pending retry state is cleared, and the stored prepared request is submitted once through the normal execution path with preparation bypassed.
semantic_action.validation: Assert the pending hinted error becomes a hint-free history item, retry/countdown state clears, and submit is called once with the stored request, non-continuation semantics, and preparation bypass.

candidate_workflows.name: add-guarded-replay-keyboard-command
candidate_workflows.title: Add a guarded keyboard command for replaying the last failed operation
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order implementation workflow that introduces an exact semantic key binding, establishes replay eligibility state, reconciles transient failure UI, and routes the shortcut to one guarded replay action.

workflow_graph.goal: A focused keyboard shortcut safely replays the exact last failed prepared operation once, while preserving normal typing, existing shortcuts, active execution flows, durable error history, and transient retry feedback.
when_to_use: A terminal or keyboard-driven interface needs an explicit shortcut to repeat the most recent failed asynchronous operation.
The application can identify and retain the exact prepared operation that failed.
The input layer already routes normalized key events through semantic command matchers and UI actions.
anti_goals: Do not make the unmodified character trigger replay or replace an existing shortcut.
Do not replay the most recent successful operation or guess a request when no failed target exists.
Do not interrupt an active response or a confirmation workflow.
Do not duplicate prompt preparation or leave transient retry hints in durable history.
Do not redesign automatic retry policy as part of adding the manual shortcut.
not_applicable_when: The operation cannot be safely or deterministically replayed from retained state.
Replay is non-idempotent or requires fresh user confirmation that the workflow cannot obtain.
The interface bypasses the normalized command-routing layer or the proposed key conflicts cannot be resolved.
Failures are already exclusively handled by an automatic retry mechanism and no manual replay affordance is desired.
inputs: A semantic command identifier and non-conflicting normalized key chord
The prepared operation payload that must be retained for replay
Explicit success/failure and active-execution state predicates
A UI action route from the focused input component to the operation controller
Transient error/hint state and durable history APIs
Matcher, input-routing, lifecycle, and replay validation harnesses
workflow_graph.entry_state: The application can submit operations and display failures, but has no semantic retry-last shortcut, retained failed-operation contract, or guarded manual replay action.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The exact shortcut dispatches one replay action; replay occurs only for an idle controller with a retained failed operation; the prior error is preserved without transient hint text; pending retry artifacts are cleared; and unrelated keys and active workflows remain unchanged.

steps.condition: The operation controller can expose the prepared payload and distinguish failed, successful, responding, and confirmation states.
steps.validation: Lifecycle tests demonstrate that only the latest failed prepared operation is eligible and active states suppress replay.

steps.condition: A failed operation is eligible and pending error or countdown UI may exist.
steps.validation: A replay test proves hint-free history preservation, clearing of pending retry state, preparation bypass, and exactly one submission of the stored payload.

steps.condition: The chosen chord is representable by the normalized matcher and is available in the focused input context.
steps.validation: Matcher tests distinguish the modified chord from plain and conflicting keys, and an input test asserts the routed replay callback is invoked exactly once.

validation_ladder: Static contract: confirm the semantic command, default chord, UI action type, provider wiring, and input dispatch branch agree.
Matcher unit tests: prove the intended modifier/key combination matches while the plain key and nearby existing shortcut do not.
Input routing test: send the terminal key sequence and assert exactly one replay action call; verify normal typing and existing shortcut behavior remain intact.
Lifecycle unit tests: cover no failed target, prior success, active response, waiting for confirmation, and eligible failed target.
State reconciliation test: prove durable error text excludes the transient hint, pending retry artifacts clear, and the prepared payload is submitted once without re-preparation.
User-contract check: ensure shortcut discovery, documentation, and localized availability messages describe the implemented behavior.
stop_conditions: Stop if the exact failed prepared operation cannot be retained without ambiguity.
Stop if the selected key chord conflicts with an existing command in the same input context.
Stop if replay can run concurrently with active execution or confirmation.
Stop if validation cannot distinguish retrying a failed request from resubmitting arbitrary or successful input.
Stop promotion if the positive shortcut path or guarded replay operation lacks an asserting test oracle.
unresolved_or_deferred: The committed InputPrompt Ctrl+Y positive test sends the control byte but does not assert that handleRetryLastPrompt was called.
No direct useGeminiStream test in the inspected commit was found for retryLastPrompt eligibility guards, hint-free history commit, skipPreparation arguments, or exactly-once replay.
Repository tests were not executed because the supplied worktree has widespread pre-existing deletions; validation claims are based on inspected test code, not a fresh passing run.

The final implementation still maintains a separate retry_countdown item while also placing countdown text in the error hint; the intended long-term presentation contract is not fully established by this episode.

unresolved_questions: Did CI or the PR status checks pass? The evidence bundle marks status checks and review metadata unavailable.

Should manual replay bypass every preparation side effect, or only transformations already reflected in the stored prepared request? The implementation uses a single skipPreparation switch without a dedicated behavioral test.
Was the non-asserting positive Ctrl+Y InputPrompt test intentional, or did module mocking prevent verification of the dispatched callback?
